overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the notice was posted at least 48 hours ahead, and the unanticipated fishing permit topic was not reasonably anticipated, though the AG advised postponing controversial unnoticed topics.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly posted its hearing notice on a shellfish drag moratorium before voting to hold the hearing.
allegations.key_passage: Here, because the Board posted notice for the November 3, 2015 meeting at least 48 hours prior— on October 30, 2015— we find that the Board satisfied its obligations with respect to notice posting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing and voting on a commercial fishing permit that was not listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the issue of the commercial fishing permit was not reasonably anticipated by the Board at least 48 hours prior to the November 3, 2015 meeting, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing this issue.
